# CityScroll source contracts

This ledger names each civic-data source used by the live product or a committed build.
The machine-readable registry is the source of truth. A source marked **live** must expose
its contracted fields and pass its freshness limit. Manual and disabled sources are kept
visible so a webpage or broken identifier cannot be mistaken for a working feed.
Acquisition status and product delivery tier are independent of warehouse retention and
production D1 `source_records` coverage. Warehouse snapshots therefore document product
materialization only; they never imply immutable observation coverage.

Live browser queries use a five-minute cache; Worker mirrors and materialized views refresh daily. Attachment metadata uses document_links before 2025 and a polite host-side RequestDetail delta from 2025 onward because the exported column is empty in the modern era. |

## Measured freshness policies

Freshness limits are source-specific. The entries below record the publisher metadata
measurement used to calibrate a limit; sources without a measured entry retain their
existing contract limit until a cadence measurement is available.

| Source | Limit | Measurement |
|---|---:|---|
| Mandatory Inclusionary Housing | 120 days | 31-day monthly cadence + 48-day observed metadata lag + 41-day margin = 120-day limit |

## External-award coverage

The runtime registry maps 13 City Record agency names to 12 distinct Authorities Budget Office authorities (12 distinct dataset-and-authority pulls) across `8w5p-k45m`, `d84c-dk28`, `ehig-g5x3`. It also contains 1 exact NYCHA mapping and 16 explicit gaps. ABO rows remain authority-scoped: the measured residual bridge joined 1/50 notices and is stopped below the 30% usefulness and 95% precision gates, so no notice-level edge is published.

## Procurement-plan materialization

The official FY2027 Local Law 63 and Local Law 1 index pages publish per-agency XLSX
plans rather than one stable table. The host-side collector treats those index pages as
manifests: it rate-limits requests, checkpoints each workbook, records content hashes, and
normalizes plan rows into warehouse tables. Capital budget and schedule rows come separately
from `fb86-vt7u`. The production payload contains 11,566 MOCS rows and 50,000 capital-project
rows. Its six independent 100-row City Record/PASSPort bridge samples each measured 0%, so
the 30% stop rules emit no bridge edges and the dependent reader remains inert.

## Verification

Run:

```sh
node tools/verify_source_contracts.mjs
node tools/generate_source_docs.mjs --check
node tools/verify_source_contracts.mjs --live
```

The first command validates the registry against committed source-shape fixtures without
network access. Pull-request CI requires that deterministic check. A daily scheduled workflow
runs the live verifier for source type, required fields, bounded sample rows, and declared
freshness metadata; it opens or updates an issue when the upstream contract drifts. The live
check also rechecks the official MOCS index pages and the Capital Projects Dashboard, so a
publisher-shape change becomes an explicit contract review instead of silently changing product
behavior.
